The instantaneous power in an inductor is given by  
\[
p(t) = v(t) \, i(t)
\]  
and for an inductor,  
\[
v(t) = L \frac{di}{dt}.
\]  
Thus,  
\[
p(t) = L \, i(t) \, \frac{di}{dt}.
\]  
This means instantaneous power is proportional to the product of instantaneous current and the rate of change of current.  

Final answer: (A)
